decisions.reason: As a niche particle-therapy water phantom that was only briefly highlighted and already had market-access limits at launch, it likely offers lower remaining option value than its support and portfolio costs by 2022.
This small-volume ionization chamber stayed fully marketed through 2019, fits the firm's core dosimetry capabilities, and is relatively inexpensive to retain as part of a broader chamber portfolio.
It is close to the firm's core business and cheap to carry, but the presence of another small-volume chamber raises some rationalization risk if the two overlap too much.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a broad-use, core product for this type of German medical-physics supplier and likely remains worth keeping in the catalog.
The chamber for relative dosimetry complements the firm's QA offering and likely still has enough specialist demand to justify keeping it unless sales proved clearly weak.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, well-fitting extension of the firm's measurement portfolio and should have low incremental carrying cost once launched.
